Scenarios.Scenario: Open, update, switch, and close an artifact's details panel
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening synchronously creates the selected artifact's model and panel and renders available snapshot data. Detail leases are acquired asynchronously; their completion gates populated state lists, not creation of the panel or Autopilot controls. Observable updates request the existing animation-frame-coalesced layout. Switching artifacts or closing disposes the prior panel and model.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request and release live detail subscriptions over the selected integration transport, backed by agent-host transport or the local host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: D subscription requests for a new panel on the protocol-backed path, not one request per list row; corresponding release requests on disposal. Stable leases are not reacquired by routine view updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same D deduplicated subscriptions and disposal requests occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial responses gate detailed list content; asynchronous lease acquisition does not block initial control construction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire provider-owned detail models, which may perform provider-specific resource access.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one underlying model per binding/detailsId while references remain; provider-specific network or filesystem request counts depend on unchanged provider implementation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical provider acquisition, reference sharing, and last-reference cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider initialization and updates determine when detail data becomes available.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read DOM geometry, computed style, and scroll height, then size the panel and lists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing initial layout and coalesced layouts after updates, resize, or external scroll; the diff does not introduce geometry reads or per-row layout calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same layout scheduling and measurements; only bounded header/control styling and DOM structure change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs on the renderer thread before the panel is painted at its updated size.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected artifact per context view; G contributions with displayed automation options, R total displayed rules, and D distinct (integrationId, detailsId) pairs after main/section/list deduplication. Changed construction adds one wrapper, label, UUID, and hover registration per group, not per detail item or update.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All distinct detail lease acquisitions start asynchronously without a new limiter or serialization change. UI update work is synchronous; pending layout is coalesced to one scheduled animation-frame callback. Only the selected artifact's panel is active in each context view.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ArtifactAutopilot retains groups by integration ID and rules by ID/policy presence, updating rather than reconstructing stable controls. Removed groups/rules are disposed. Details leases deduplicate references in the model, and ArtifactBinding shares provider detail models by detailsId while references remain. Last-reference release removes the provider cache entry. Reopening may reacquire details; the diff changes neither successful nor failed acquisition behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor ownership, keyed reuse, removal/disposal, detail deduplication, provider sharing, and layout coalescing are directly visible in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual provider count, detail sizes, and provider-specific I/O latency are not measured. The added per-group DOM and listener work is small and bounded; no newly expensive scaling path is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added controls are constructed once per retained group and their hover registrations are owned by group disposal. Existing async subscriptions and layout paths retain their prior multiplicity.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enable or disable all available Autopilot rules using the switch or its new visible label
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The native label targets the existing button. One switch onChange calls setGroup, which collects changed rule values and saves them as a single integration-level write. The model presents unconfirmed values immediately. Saving completion waits for configure, persistence, and existing disabled-run revocation; focus restoration waits on that promise.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send one configure request containing the selected integration's changed values and await acknowledgement on protocol-backed models.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one request for E changed options in a group; zero for a no-op; additional rapidly issued changes retain existing integration-level coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The master switch already called the same setGroup/save/write path with the same grouping. The new label provides another native activation target, not an additional configure dispatch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Acknowledgement gates save completion, not immediate optimistic display.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Clone ledger state, compare it, and JSON-serialize a changed ledger before storage commit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One transaction per configure plus unchanged execution bookkeeping; unchanged transactions skip serialization and storage write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical whole-ledger transaction behavior and idempotent-write suppression.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialization and storage commit precede publication of confirmed ledger state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read IndexedDB ledger on initialization and commit changes with compareAndSwap on the browser-local path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initialization read per store instance and one commit for each changed ledger transaction, not one per changed option.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initialization caching and grouped storage commits were required for the original switch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Persistence gates configure completion on the local runtime.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cancel applicable running automations, with existing prompt recovery/cancellation where necessary, and wake the executor after configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing serial cleanup for affected unsettled automation runs of the selected binding; provider/runtime-specific downstream calls are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same revocation and executor wake for the same group configuration change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Revocation is awaited by configure; subsequent automation execution remains owned by the existing executor.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: E changed options within the chosen integration, not all providers and not all artifact rows. One logical toggle produces one values record and normally one configure call, subject to existing coalescing and no-op suppression. Disabled-run cleanup scales with applicable unsettled runs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: SequencerByKey serializes writes per integration. Different integration keys can proceed independently. Ledger transactions are additionally serialized by the store's sequencer. Disabled-run revocation awaits cancellations serially as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prepared policies and unconfirmed values retain their existing semantics. Values equal to current configuration are filtered before configure. Changes arriving during an in-flight integration write are combined for the next write; the new label does not bypass these mechanisms.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the switch callback is unchanged, label.htmlFor uses the existing button ID, the presentation test demonstrates one configuration per activation, and the model explicitly groups values and sequences/coalesces writes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Ledger size, transport latency, and number of active automations are unmeasured. These can make the existing write expensive but do not establish a diff-caused increase.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. A new activation surface preserves the existing single grouped write rather than introducing per-rule fan-out or duplicate submission.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand or collapse Autopilot/Activities, choose policies, navigate by keyboard, and resize the details panel
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Heading activation updates remembered expansion and triggers the existing observable render/layout path. Policy selection opens the existing quick picker; selecting while off updates prepared policy locally, while selecting for an enabled rule uses the existing grouped save path. Focus and resize use unchanged geometry/reveal code.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Measure geometry and scroll position, resize lists, and reveal keyboard-focused content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing focus/reveal operations and coalesced resize/update layout; no newly added geometry read loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical layout/reveal call paths and scheduling, with the old spacing and focus outline styles.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These renderer-thread operations precede updated layout/scroll presentation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible provider groups and rules in one details panel, plus the bounded state/Activities list layout. Expansion still does not change provider acquisition count. CSS changes adjust spacing, chevron margins, and pointer-versus-keyboard focus outlines.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: DOM updates are synchronous on the UI thread. Context view relayout is coalesced at the next animation frame. Existing per-rule picking suppression and per-integration write sequencing remain unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Expansion and prepared policy choices remain in ArtifactDetailsViewState. Stable group/rule controls remain reused. No new cache or negative-cache behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed CSS introduces neither live filters/animations nor geometry reads; the heading exclusion and hover-feedback listeners retain one registration per control; model expansion and policy code are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Different viewport widths can alter wrapping and natural panel height. No evidence shows repeated relayout, a feedback loop, or materially larger work due to these ordinary spacing changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Existing layout work is not moved onto a hotter path, and eager creation of rule controls while collapsed predates this PR.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hover the new Toggle All label or read artifact accessibility help
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The label hover resolves the existing plain-text group description on mouseover and uses the hover service's delayed display. Accessibility Help generates the existing localized text with the revised name; the changed wording performs no new service read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register a mouseover listener and map entry, then construct a HoverWidget on actual display using the already available description string.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extra listener/map entry per group for the label; displayed hover work follows pointer events, not the total number of registered groups. Registrations are disposed with their owner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The master switch already had description hover registration; the label did not exist. The PR adds one equivalent target without adding resource fetching or changing switch hover frequency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Registration is small constructor work; hover widget work is deferred until hover display and does not gate panel opening.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One additional hover target per displayed provider group, rather than per rule or artifact history item. Hover display is driven by user interaction with the current target.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hover interaction uses the existing delayed-hover mechanism and replacement lifecycle, not concurrent preconstruction of a widget for every registered target. Help content is generated synchronously on request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Hover registration adds a target to the service map; its registered disposable removes that target and listener when the group is removed or panel disposed. Current hover identity checks and top-level hover replacement are unchanged. No network-backed hover content or new long-lived cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: setupDelayedHover only registers listeners/map state, returns a disposable, and defers widget creation. The group registers that disposable and supplies existing plain text.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Pointer event frequency and exact hover rendering time are unmeasured. The added registration is bounded by displayed groups and has explicit cleanup.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This is small, intentionally added interaction work with lazy display and bounded lifecycle, not eager heavyweight work or unbounded retention.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass against base ddbdd50a9ed1f9dc32e4fbadcf950b290e7d35b4. Inspected the complete six-file inventory and every diff page, and traced changed UI construction, update/disposal ownership, hover behavior, layout, grouped configuration, and detail-subscription/persistence boundaries. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or concrete regression fix qualifies for reporting. Static review; no measured performance results.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
